title: Derived support sections commute with etale-proetale direct image
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], on small representatives of the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Derived categories are unbounded localizations at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $C\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Write $H^	au_{T,C}=R\Gamma_C(T_	au,-)$ for the right derived kernel-of-restriction functor [def-pur-support-cohomology], on all complexes computed with K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. For every $N\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$b_{C,N}:H^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}(R
u_{T,*}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}(N).$$
Its normalization is the identity, on a K-injective representative $J$ of $N$, between the two complexes $\ker(J(T)	o J(T\setminus C))$. This isomorphism commutes with forgetting supports and with restriction to every open $V\subseteq T$, using $C_V=C	imes_T V$ and the canonical restriction identifications for $R
u_*$ and the two support functors. These restriction identifications also intertwine the derived comparison adjunction units under the canonical inverse-image restriction comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. For $C=T$, $b_{T,N}$ is the final-object comparison $R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},R
u_{T,*}N)\cong R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{proet}},N)$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: the comparison functor preserves derived support sections via the direct-image/K-injective kernel identity.

proof.text: Put $U=T\setminus C$. Write $\mathcal A_\tau(T)=\operatorname{Mod}(T_\tau,A)$ and $Q$ for localization of complexes. The comparison adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] acts on these ordinary constant-$A$ modules. Its inverse image is exact: on underlying abelian sheaves this is [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]; kernels and cokernels of module sheaves carry the induced $A$-actions, so their underlying abelian sheaves compute these kernels and cokernels. Thus exactness is detected after forgetting the action. On small site representatives, [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] provides K-injective resolutions for both topologies. The kernel-of-restriction functors of [def-pur-support-cohomology] are additive: a map acts by restriction of its section map to the kernel. Additive functors preserve chain homotopies and mapping cones (finite sums with the signed differential). Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] applies to their termwise functors followed by $Q$, giving the stated unbounded support functors; the same applies to $\nu_{T,*}$. This explicitly extends the bounded-below convention of the support definition, rather than assuming that definition already supplies an unbounded theorem.

Choose a K-injective representative $J$ of $N$. Since $
u_T^*$ is exact and left adjoint to $
u_{T,*}$, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] implies that $
u_{T,*}J$ is K-injective on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. Hence $R
u_{T,*}N$ is represented by $
u_{T,*}J$, and its etale support functor may be computed using that very representative, without resolving again [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. By the explicit direct-image definition [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], in every degree $(
u_{T,*}J)(T)=J(T)$ and $(
u_{T,*}J)(U)=J(U)$, and the restriction arrows are the same arrows of $J$. Therefore
$$\Gamma_C(T_{\mathrm{et}},
u_{T,*}J)=\ker(J(T)	o J(U))=\Gamma_C(T_{\mathrm{proet}},J)$$
as complexes of $A$-modules, with identical differentials. Localizing the identity on this complex defines $b_{C,N}$ and proves both its invertibility and its required normalization.

proof.text: For a morphism $N\to N'$ and K-injective representatives $J,J'$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents it by a unique homotopy class of chain maps $f:J\to J'$. Applying either side of the kernel identity in Step 2 gives the same map on kernels, since $(\nu_*f)(T)=f(T)$ and $(\nu_*f)(U)=f(U)$. Additivity implies that a chain homotopy restricts to a chain homotopy on these kernels: its degree maps are sheaf morphisms and thus commute with restriction. Hence the equality is independent of the chosen chain map. Changing K-injective representatives gives a homotopy equivalence by the same cited lemma, and the equality commutes with it. This proves independence of representative and naturality of $b$, with the canonical derived-functor resolution identifications.

proof.text:
Let $j:V\hookrightarrow T$ be any open immersion, and put $U_V=U\cap V$. On the etale site use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]; on the pro-etale site use [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] and [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction]. Thus $j_	au^*$ is restriction to the slice over $V$, with constant coefficient rings canonically identified. In the etale case the abelian restriction isomorphism respects the $A$-actions because it is natural for each scalar endomorphism, so it applies to the module sheaves as well. By [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], $J|_V$ and $(
u_{T,*}J)|_V$ are K-injective. For every etale object $W	o V$,
$$((
u_{T,*}J)|_V)(W)=J(W)=(
u_{V,*}(J|_V))(W),$$
with identical restrictions and scalar actions. This identity therefore computes the canonical derived restriction identification
$$ho_N:j_{\mathrm{et}}^*R
u_{T,*}N\xrightarrow{\sim}R
u_{V,*}j_{\mathrm{proet}}^*N.$$
No quasi-compactness of $V$, boundedness of $N$, or etale-origin hypothesis was used.

source.place: Tag 08FI (lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open); sites.tex Section 00XZ (section-localize); restriction along the etale/pro-etale inclusion

proof.text:
Forgetting supports on $J$ is the inclusion $\ker(J(T)\to J(U))\hookrightarrow J(T)$. Restriction to $V$ is the map
$$\ker(J(T)\to J(U))\longrightarrow\ker(J(V)\to J(U_V)),\qquad s\longmapsto s|_V.$$
It lands in the indicated kernel since $s|_{U_V}=(s|_U)|_{U_V}=0$. By Step 4 the displayed kernels also compute both support functors after open restriction. Step 2 identifies the etale and pro-etale complexes and all the arrows here by identities. Thus the forgetting-supports and open-restriction squares commute degree by degree, and hence in the derived category. Naturality and independence of resolution follow from Step 3 applied to these same section and kernel maps. Successive open restrictions use $s|_{V'}=(s|_V)|_{V'}$ for $V'\subset V$, so the identifications are coherent under further restriction as well.

u_{T,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}
u_{V,*}j_{\mathrm{proet}}^*$ be the sectionwise identity of Step 4, $((
u_{T,*}G)|_V)(W)=G(W)=(
u_{V,*}(G|_V))(W)$ for etale $W	o V$. These are exactly the maps $a$ and $c$ of [lem-pur-comparison-pullback-open-unit], whose restriction identifications are those used in Step 4. That lemma gives, for every etale module sheaf $F$ on $T$,
$$
u_{V,*}(a_F)\,c_{
u_T^*F}\,j_{\mathrm{et}}^*(\eta^T_F)=\eta^V_{j_{\mathrm{et}}^*F}.$$
All maps in it are morphisms of module sheaves, so this is an equality for the specified module adjunctions, not only for sets. Naturality of $a$ and $c$ in their arguments is part of the cited statements.

proof.text:
The exact functors $
u^*$ and open restriction descend termwise to unbounded derived categories by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. The derived adjunction $
u_T^*\dashv R
u_{T,*}$ is the bijection, natural in both variables, for $M=QP$ and $N=QJ$ with $J$ K-injective:
$$\operatorname{Hom}_D(
u_T^*M,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(
u_T^*P,J)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(P,
u_{T,*}J)=\operatorname{Hom}_D(M,R
u_{T,*}N).$$
The outer equalities are [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], as $
u_T^*P$ represents $
u_T^*M$ and $
u_{T,*}J$ is K-injective representing $R
u_{T,*}N$ (Step 2); the middle one is the degreewise underived adjunction, which preserves homotopies by additivity. This is the canonical adjunction of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors]: $
u_T^*$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms, so its pro-system is constant; K-injective resolutions are cofinal among quasi-isomorphisms out of a complex, with unique homotopy classes of maps under it by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], so the ind-system of $
u_{T,*}$ has value $
u_{T,*}J$ and the colimit bijection reduces to the chain displayed. Choose a K-injective resolution $r:
u_T^*P	o J$. Under the chain, $Qr$ corresponds to the class of
$$P\xrightarrow{\eta^T_P}
u_{T,*}
u_T^*P\xrightarrow{
u_{T,*}r}
u_{T,*}J,$$
the derived unit at $M$ after the identification $Qr$. By Step 4, $J|_V$ is K-injective and $r'=r|_V\circ a_P^{-1}:
u_V^*(P|_V)	o J|_V$ is a resolution. Step 6 and naturality of $c$ give
$$
u_{V,*}(r')\eta^V_{P|_V}=
u_{V,*}(r|_V)c_{
u_T^*P}j_{\mathrm{et}}^*(\eta^T_P).$$
These represent the two restricted derived units, so $ho$ intertwines them under $a$, for arbitrary unbounded $M$.

proof.text: Finally take $C=T$. The complement is empty, and a sheaf of $A$-modules has zero sections over the empty scheme by the sheaf axiom for the empty covering. Hence the kernel in Step 2 is simply $J(T)$. The same K-injective representatives compute $R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},R\nu_{T,*}N)$ and $R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{proet}},N)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. On them $b_{T,N}$ is the identity $(\nu_{T,*}J)(T)=J(T)$, which is precisely the final-object comparison, with the same normalization as the comparison for general $C$.
